pages.text:

Lattice Semiconductor stock, semiconductors, FPGA, Q2 2026 results, Nasdaq, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Lattice Semiconductor stock stood at USD 122.22 on Nasdaq on September 24, 2026, up 0.46 percent from the prior close. The semiconductor company delivered record Q2 2026 revenue of USD 201.1 million, giving the stock a fresh earnings anchor despite its position 22.2 percent below the 52-week high of USD 157.01.
According to Yahoo Finance, revenue in Q2 2026 rose 62 percent year over year and 18 percent sequentially to USD 201 million. The sequential increase from USD 170.9 million in Q1 2026 shows that the growth was not limited to an easy annual comparison.
The earnings quality was equally important. Non-GAAP EPS reached USD 0.53 in Q2 2026, more than 120 percent above the prior-year level and USD 0.09 above the consensus estimate of USD 0.44, according to Zacks.
Lattice guided to adjusted EPS of USD 0.54 to USD 0.58 for Q3 2026, while revenue guidance stood at USD 245 million to USD 265 million, according to Yahoo Finance. The midpoint of the EPS range is USD 0.56, which would exceed the Q2 result by USD 0.03 if achieved.
Operating leverage is the central financial variable. Standardized Q2 data show operating profit of USD 22.353 million and an operating margin of 11 percent, compared with USD 26.068 million and 15 percent in Q1 2026, so revenue growth has yet to translate into a sequential margin expansion.
Lattice Semiconductor had a market capitalization of USD 16.745 billion as of September 24, 2026, with a 52-week range of USD 60.50 to USD 157.01. The USD 122.22 Nasdaq price therefore sits materially below the yearly high, while the Q3 revenue range of USD 245 million to USD 265 million provides the next concrete test for the growth narrative.

Shares of semiconductor designer Lattice Semiconductor (NASDAQ:LSCC) jumped 5.7% in the afternoon session after the company launched its Mach-N2 FPGA line and Prompt AI development tool for data center security and efficiency, alongside a newly disclosed $94.74 million stake by Bank of America.

Peer chipmaker stocks advanced in tandem during the session as trading reflected a wider industry rotation.

As the craze of earnings season draws to a close, here's a look back at some of the most exciting (and some less so) results from Q2. Today, we are looking at processors and graphics chips stocks, starting with Lattice Semiconductor (NASDAQ:LSCC).
The biggest demand drivers for processors (CPUs) and graphics chips at the moment are secular trends related to 5G and Internet of Things, autonomous driving, and high performance computing in the data center space, specifically around AI and machine learning. Like all semiconductor companies, digital chip makers exhibit a degree of cyclicality, driven by supply and demand imbalances and exposure to PC and Smartphone product cycles.
The 9 processors and graphics chips stocks we track reported a very strong Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 6.3% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 6.8% above.
Thankfully, share prices of the companies have been resilient as they are up 5.6% on average since the latest earnings results.

Lattice Semiconductor reported revenues of $201.1 million, up 62.2% year on year. This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 8.6%. Overall, it was a stunning quarter for the company with a beat of analysts' EPS and operating income estimates.

Investor expectations, however, were likely higher than Wall Street's published projections, leaving some wishing for even better results (analysts' consensus estimates are those published by big banks and advisory firms, not the investors who make buy and sell decisions).
